title: Telemetry Mosaic: Adaptive Performance Inspector for Model Routes
creator: Aditi Rao
description: Design a modular, adaptive inspector panel (Telemetry Mosaic) for the Redwood Console that surfaces per-model and per-route performance signals. The inspector should support quick diagnosis flows (latency spikes, throughput drops, token cost regressions) and deep-dive charting (quantiles, microtraces, token flow) while remaining compact enough for side-panel use during rollouts. Deliverables: annotated wireframes, responsive Figma prototype, detailed chart spec lines for engineering, and a dev handoff doc listing component variants and accessibility notes.
acceptance_criteria: Side-panel inspector shows a compact summary row (avg latency, p95, rps, token-cost) for selected route and model
Clicking a metric expands to a focused chart area with drilldown controls (time window, percentile selector, compare-to-baseline)
Chart spec includes rendering guidance for low-cardinality vs high-cardinality routes and fallback visuals for sparse data
Prototype supports toggling between absolute and normalized cost views and overlays rollout phases (canary/cutover)
Design handoff includes tokens/spacing, color tokens (accessible contrast), and component states for error/empty/loading
decisions: Use a two-tier interaction: compact summary row + expanded canvas area. Default is compact to preserve space in Console.
Primary latency visual will be a quantile ribbon (p50/p90/p95/p99) with a selectable baseline overlay rather than multiple separate sparkline tiles.
Token flow will be represented as a Sankey-like microflow when route variance is high; otherwise fallback to stacked area by token type (input/system/output)
Cost attribution will default to a waterfall breakdown with hover-to-expand for per-component token costs (prompt, completion, safety checks)
For routes with <50 requests in selected window show a sparse-data CTA and a single time-series with confidence shading instead of quantiles
tradeoffs: Quantile ribbon is denser information than separate percentiles but requires careful axis labeling — chosen for faster outlier detection
Sankey microflow communicates routing/token-path complexity but is heavier to render; only enable for selected routes or when user expands the token view
Showing both cost and latency on same canvas simplifies correlation but risks clutter; decided to provide synchronized small-multiples with shared crosshair instead
components: ExpandedCanvas (chart area with tabs: Latency, Throughput, Tokens, Cost, Traces)
MicrotraceSwimlane (sampled request traces aligned with time windows)
chart_spec_lines: QuantileRibbonChart: x=time, y=latency(ms); render median line, shaded bands for p50-p90 and p90-p99; baseline overlay in dashed line; show token-count annotated on hover; default aggregation=1m
ThroughputHeatmap: x=time bucket (5m), y=hour-of-day or route bucket; color scale linear for RPS with log option; tooltips show exact RPS and request count; missing data hatched
TokenFlowMicroSankey: source=input tokens, mid=system/prompt transforms, sink=completion tokens; width=token count; collapse small flows <2% into 'other'; animated transitions on window change
CostWaterfall: stacked bars per cost component (compute, storage, prompts, safety) with cumulative line; hovering a bar shows per-token cost and sample request ids for traces

MicrotraceSwimlane: rows=sampled requests, x=time in ms, color by stage (enqueue, compute, kv-cache, kernel); align swimlane rows to the quantile chart crosshair; allow expanding a single trace to full trace view
BaselineCompare: when compare mode active render diff-sparkline under main chart (green=improvement, red=regression) and show absolute delta and % change in header
